chain.title: Start with One Resource
chain.desc: Make a one-compartment drawer and assign a bulk material. Learn its front-face insert and extract interactions before adding automation.

chain.title: Store a Pair of Materials
chain.desc: Try a two-compartment drawer for paired outputs. Each slot has its own item assignment; plan which materials should share a block.

chain.title: Increase the Capacity
chain.desc: Install a Copper Upgrade in a drawer that is filling quickly. Check the new capacity before increasing the connected farm's production.

chain.title: Expand the Same Storage Route
chain.desc: Make a Gold Upgrade through the installed recipe. Higher storage upgrades build on the capacity branch rather than changing item assignments.

chain.title: Room for Large Production Runs
chain.desc: Upgrade high-volume storage to Diamond capacity. Keep lower-volume resources in cheaper drawers where that is enough.

chain.title: Finish the Capacity Branch
chain.desc: Use the installed recipe to reach the Netherite upgrade. Confirm the drawer's capacity and keep an overflow plan for continuous production.

chain.title: Several Forms of One Resource
chain.desc: Put a supported resource in a Compacting Drawer. The related compacted forms share one stored quantity, using the installed compacting recipes.

chain.title: Give Fluids Their Own Drawer
chain.desc: Build a Fluid Drawer and connect an appropriate fluid transfer method. Item drawers and fluid drawers serve different inventories.

chain.title: A Hub for the Drawer Room
chain.desc: Build a Storage Controller as the network access point. Drawers must be linked; proximity alone is not the entire setup.

chain.title: Assign Drawers to the Controller
chain.desc: Use the Linking Tool to select the controller and link the intended drawers. Check its mode and range before connecting a large area.

chain.title: Lock and Configure the Drawers
chain.desc: Use the Configuration Tool to adjust supported drawer settings such as locking. Make assignments predictable before routing mixed outputs.

chain.title: Another Network Access Point
chain.desc: Link a Controller Extension to the network for additional access. Use it where a second machine connection is more convenient.

chain.title: Pull from the Source
chain.desc: Configure a Puller Upgrade toward the source inventory. Start with a small transfer test to confirm its side and rate.

chain.title: Supply the Next Machine
chain.desc: Configure a Pusher Upgrade toward a destination. Match the stored material to the machine's input instead of sending every drawer's contents indiscriminately.

chain.title: Decide What May Overflow
chain.desc: Use a Void Upgrade only for an output you can afford to discard. Excess beyond capacity is deleted rather than stored elsewhere.

chain.title: Connect a Real Production Loop
chain.desc: Link assigned drawers, route an actual machine or farm output into them, and retrieve the materials through the controller. Confirm after repeated transfers work.

content_revision: 2026-10-07: explicit branches, operational guidance, no collection filler

coverage.scope: Bulk and fluid drawers, actual controller linking, capacity upgrades and working item transfer.
coverage.limitations: Recipe quantities, enabled content and progression settings may be changed by the installed pack.
coverage.verification_detail: Item models, entity language identifiers, dimension data, recipes and bundled guide text where present were inspected; this is data verification, not a Minecraft playthrough.

notes: Each requires list is intentional. Empty lists are independent entry routes. Links describe guided progression or demonstrated recipe/boss gates, not an assertion that every dependency is a game-enforced lock. Runtime scanning still filters unavailable items and entities.
